newsitem.title: ESTONIA: EESTI GAAS TO DISCUSS LISTING IN AUGUST.
newsitem.headline: EESTI GAAS TO DISCUSS LISTING IN AUGUST.

text.p: Eesti Gaas, the natural gas distribution company in Estonia, will discuss listing its shares on the Tallinn bourse in August, the company chairman said on Friday.
The Estonian Privatization Agency will privatize 12.33 percent of the company's shares in a public offer for vouchers in May or June.
"If the shares are sold, then we are going to discuss it (the listing) at the next board meeting on August 20," Aarne Saar, chairman, told a news conference.
Eesti Gaas has not officially discussed the listing, because 25 percent of its shares are not in public yet, Saar added.

The company is mostly privatised with the state holding a 39.33 percent stake in the company. Gazprom, the Russian gas company, holds 30.64 pecent of the shares, Germany's Ruhrgas hoas 14.69 percent and small investors hold 15.34 percent.
Eesti Gaas share holders on Friday approved the proposal to pay dividends worth 3.9 million kroons from its net profit of 47.4 million kroons in 1996.
Eesti Gaas' board reduced the profit estimate of 20 million kroons for 1997 to break-even, Saar said, adding it was due to the strenghtening of the U.S. dollar.
The minimum profit number is also related to large investments the company plans this year as it wants to increase its markets, Saar said.
Eesti Gaas will invest 63 million kroons this year, compared to 15.9 million kroons last year.
